_description: BoxTrack wizard suggestion data. Import via Settings > Wizard Data to update.

packing: Pack one room completely before starting another.
Label every box on the sides, not just the top — boxes get stacked.
Take a photo of the inside before you tape it shut.
Pack heavy items (books, tools) in small boxes. Light items in large boxes.
Use your linens and towels as padding for fragile items.
Mark your essentials box clearly — you'll need it on night one.
Number your boxes and keep a master list of what's in each.
Leave out one set of bedding, toiletries, and a change of clothes per person.
moving_day: Load heaviest boxes first, against the truck walls.
Keep essentials box in your car, not the truck.
Take photos of furniture placement in the truck — insurance.
Load items for the last room to be unpacked first.
Keep box labels facing out so you can read them without moving boxes.
Mattresses load last and come off first. Stand them upright.
settling: Unpack essentials box first — kitchen basics, toiletries, bedding.
Set up beds before anything else. You'll be exhausted.
Unpack one room fully before starting the next.
Check each box against your inventory as you unpack.
Don't rush to hang pictures — live in the space a week first.
Flatten and bundle boxes as you go to keep the space walkable.

boxes.label: Everyday Dishes
boxes.tip: Wrap plates vertically like records — they survive better than stacked flat.

boxes.label: Pots & Pans
boxes.tip: Nest pots inside each other with paper between. Pack lids separately — they rattle and crack.

boxes.label: Cutlery & Utensils
boxes.tip: Bundle cutlery in sets and wrap in a tea towel. Mark the tray if it travels separately.

boxes.label: Small Appliances
boxes.tip: Take photos of appliance cords and settings before packing. Original boxes are ideal if you kept them.

boxes.label: Pantry & Dry Goods
boxes.tip: Pack dry goods in a dedicated box and label it PANTRY — UPRIGHT ONLY. Seal any open packages.

boxes.label: Kitchen Extras
boxes.tip: Cleaning supplies and pantry items pack well together — both can go in the kitchen first.

boxes.label: Books & Media
boxes.tip: Books are heavy. Use small boxes and mix heavy/light. Spines down or standing upright — never on the pages.

boxes.label: Electronics & AV
boxes.tip: Photo the back of your TV and receiver before unplugging. Use coloured tape to label cables.

boxes.label: Soft Furnishings & Decor
boxes.tip: Wrap frames and mirrors in moving blankets and mark FRAGILE GLASS. Keep all hardware in a labelled bag taped to the frame.

boxes.label: Bedding & Linen
boxes.tip: Use a large bin bag inside the box to keep bedding clean. Pack one set out separately for the first night.

boxes.label: Clothing
boxes.tip: Wardrobe boxes let hanging clothes travel without folding. For everything else, vacuum bags save space.

boxes.label: Toys
boxes.tip: Let kids pack their own comfort items in a backpack they carry themselves. It gives them agency during the move.

boxes.label: Kids Bedding
boxes.tip: Set up kids rooms first on moving day. Familiar surroundings help them settle.

boxes.label: Toiletries
boxes.tip: Put toiletries in a large zip-lock bag inside the box — one leak can ruin everything around it.

boxes.label: Bathroom Extras
boxes.tip: Pack medicines and prescriptions in your essentials bag — not in the moving truck.

boxes.label: Electronics
boxes.tip: Back up your computer before the move. Transport laptops in a padded bag in your car, not the truck.

boxes.label: Important Documents
boxes.tip: Documents should travel in your car, not the truck. Use a lockable document bag or fireproof pouch.

boxes.label: Hand Tools
boxes.tip: Pack tools in their original cases if possible. Drain all fuel from power tools before moving.

moving_day_checklist.label: Utilities transferred / connected at new home
Address updated with bank, employer, post
Keys to new home in hand
Essentials box packed and set aside
Kids and pets arranged for moving day
Documents, valuables, and medications in your car
Appliances disconnected and ready to move
Final walkthrough of old home completed
Meter readings taken at both properties

settling_checklist.label: Bathrooms stocked with toiletries and towels
Locks checked, alarm set up if applicable
Empty boxes broken down or donated

packing: Heaviest items on the floor against the back wall — never on top of lighter ones.
Label every box on all four sides — you will stack them and only see the sides.
Leave a central aisle down the middle so you can reach things without unloading.
Items you might need sooner go nearest the door.
Use uniform box sizes — they stack more securely and use vertical space better.
Stand mattresses upright against the side wall, never flat — they warp.
Disassemble furniture to save space. Tape hardware bags to the piece they belong to.
Wrap upholstered furniture in plastic wrap or moving blankets — moisture and dust.
Climate-sensitive items (electronics, wood furniture, art, photos) go furthest from the door.
Fill boxes completely — partial boxes collapse under weight.
Take a photo of your layout before you close the door.
Keep a numbered master list that matches your box labels.
Cedar blocks and silica gel packets protect clothing and soft goods from pests and moisture.
Never store flammable liquids, food, or plants in a storage locker.
Pallets or wooden boards off the floor protect boxes from ground moisture.

boxes.label: Christmas
boxes.tip: Ornament storage boxes with individual cells prevent breakage. Wrap glass ornaments in tissue paper.

boxes.label: Seasonal Clothing
boxes.tip: Clean all clothing before storing. Dirty clothes attract pests. Vacuum bags save significant space and protect from moisture.

boxes.label: Camping & Hiking
boxes.tip: Store sleeping bags uncompressed in a large cotton sack — long-term compression kills the loft.

boxes.label: Cycling
boxes.tip: Hang bikes vertically to save floor space. Deflate tyres slightly for long-term storage to reduce sidewall stress.

boxes.label: Water Sports
boxes.tip: Rinse and fully dry all water sports gear before storing — mould and mildew build quickly in fabric.

boxes.label: Winter Sports
boxes.tip: Store skis horizontally on a wall rack or vertically in a ski bag. Wax before storing to prevent edge rust.

boxes.label: Furniture Hardware
boxes.tip: Tape hardware bags directly to the furniture piece with a label. Never store hardware separately — you will not remember which piece it belongs to.

boxes.label: Bedding & Linens
boxes.tip: Store bedding in breathable cotton bags or vacuum bags — never plastic bins which trap moisture.

boxes.label: Power Tools
boxes.tip: Drain all fuel from petrol-powered tools before storage. Loosen drill chucks to prevent spring fatigue.

boxes.label: Garden Tools
boxes.tip: Clean and oil all garden tools before storing. Hang long-handled tools vertically — store flat and the handles warp.

boxes.label: Books & Media
boxes.tip: Pack books spine-down or standing upright — never on their pages. Seal boxes well to prevent silverfish damage.

boxes.label: Valuables & Sentimental
boxes.tip: Photos and home videos are irreplaceable. Consider digitising before putting into long-term storage. Store in a climate-controlled unit if possible.

packing: Finish one zone completely before starting another — partial organisation is discouraging.
Everything needs a home. If it does not have one: donate, discard, or designate a spot.
Like goes with like. Group by use and activity, not by object type.
The most-used items go at waist height. Rarely-used items go high or low.
Clear containers let you see contents without opening — worth the cost.
Label bins on the front, not the top — bins get stacked.
Seasonal items go in the hardest-to-reach spots.
Leave 20% empty space in every storage area — life expands to fill all available space otherwise.
Before you buy storage, measure twice. Before you organise, purge first.

boxes.label: Pantry
boxes.tip: Group pantry items by category: baking, canned goods, grains, sauces. Decant into uniform containers for a calmer shelf.

boxes.label: Media & Electronics
boxes.tip: Label every cable with masking tape and a marker. A cable box with labelled velcro ties saves hours of future frustration.

boxes.label: Wardrobe
boxes.tip: Organise by category then by colour within each category. Turn all hangers backwards — after 6 months, donate anything not touched.

boxes.label: Toys
boxes.tip: Involve kids in the organisation. Bins at their height labelled with pictures (not just words) build habits.

boxes.label: Tools
boxes.tip: A pegboard for hand tools is the single highest-ROI garage organisation investment. Outline each tool with a marker so things go back in the right spot.

boxes.label: Hardware & Fasteners
boxes.tip: Sort fasteners into a parts organiser with small drawers. Label each drawer. Worth every penny.

boxes.label: Cleaning Supplies
boxes.tip: Keep one cleaning caddy stocked and portable — it travels room to room and nothing gets left behind.

boxes.label: Documents & Filing
boxes.tip: Scan important documents and store in cloud backup. Paper copies in a fireproof folder or safe.

packing: Roll clothes instead of folding — saves space and reduces wrinkles.
Pack your heaviest items at the bottom of your bag, closest to your back.
Wear your bulkiest items on the plane — coat, boots, heaviest jumper.
Pack a day-bag inside your main bag so you have one for day trips.
Toiletries in a clear zip-lock bag that passes security easily.
Copy important documents and email them to yourself before you leave.
Chargers and cables in one dedicated pouch — you will use them every day.
Leave 20% space for things you buy on the trip.
Always pack one full outfit in your carry-on in case luggage is delayed.
Fragile items go in the centre of the bag surrounded by soft clothing.
Check weather at your destination before packing — pack for real conditions.

boxes.label: Everyday Wear
boxes.tip: Pack clothes that mix and match. 3 bottoms + 5 tops = 15 outfits.

boxes.label: Footwear
boxes.tip: Stuff socks inside shoes to maintain shape and save space.

boxes.label: Toiletries
boxes.tip: Decant products into travel bottles. Weigh your bag before adding toiletries — liquids are heavy.

boxes.label: Documents & Money
boxes.tip: Flag your passport and medication in the app so you can always confirm which bag they are in.

boxes.label: Health & Medications
boxes.tip: Keep all medications in your carry-on, never in checked luggage.
